The Fe-rich region gave about 7× more photocurrent. #13 (Cr0.21 Fe0.59 V0.21) measured 2.01 µA, slightly more than #200 (Fe0.70, V0.11) at 1.75 µA. This suggests the best composition has moderate V (~0.2) in an Fe-rich oxide.

content.text:
I submitted **#13 (Cr 0.21, Fe 0.59, V 0.21)** as the best composition. It gave 2.01 µA, the highest of the three photocurrents I measured. The budget allowed only 3 measurements out of 201 compositions, so I can't confirm it's the best in the library.

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 52 | 0.23 / 0.28 / 0.50 | 0.28 µA |
| **13** | **0.21 / 0.59 / 0.21** | **2.01 µA** |
| 200 | 0.19 / 0.70 / 0.11 | 1.75 µA |

- **Fe-rich wins:** The two Fe-rich compositions gave about 7× more photocurrent than the V-rich #52.
- **Some V helps:** Cutting V further to 0.11 (#200) gave less photocurrent than #13, so the best point is probably Fe-rich with about 0.2 V.
- **Untested areas:** Cr-rich compositions were never measured. I passed them over because chromium oxides tend to perform poorly as photoanodes, not because of any data. I also didn't test compositions near #13 (for example #20, #83 or #149), which could be slightly better.
- **XRD unused:** None of the 5 XRD measurements were used. With only 3 photocurrent measurements, I judged phase data unlikely to change which compositions to test.
